resources.string: Log two full-tank fill-ups and your mileage, ₹/km and trends appear here.
Cost per km for this period

Fuel or charging plus running costs (service, tolls, parking and similar) in the period, divided by the kilometres driven in it. Loan EMIs and the purchase price are left out. The change compares with the period of the same length just before.

Total spent adds every fill-up and expense in the period. Distance is the odometer change; when there are fewer than two readings it is estimated from the readings around the period. Average mileage is all distance divided by all fuel across full-to-full tanks closed in the period. Cost per day is the ₹/km spend divided by the days in the period.
Your mileage dropped %1$d%% over the last 2 tanks. Check tyre pressure first, then the air filter, and whether a service is due.
You get %1$d%% of the claimed mileage: %2$s km/%3$s against %4$s claimed.
Not enough entries in this period for this chart.

Each bar is one full-to-full tank: the distance between two full fills divided by everything filled in between, partial fills included. The line is the rolling mileage of the last 3 tanks (total distance ÷ total fuel). The dashed line is the claimed figure from the vehicle settings.
Each bar is one month: fuel or charging paid (after discounts) in the dark part, every other expense in the light part, including EMIs.
The price per unit you paid at each fill-up, as entered or calculated from quantity and total.
Each point is one month: fuel and running costs divided by the kilometres driven that month. Months without enough odometer readings are left out.
Everything spent in the period, grouped by category, largest first.
Every odometer reading you logged in the period, from fill-ups and expenses.
